items.title: SQL Server Performance Office Hours Episode 68
items.author: Erik Darling (Erik Darling Data)
items.summary:
In this video, I tackle some of the most pressing questions submitted by the SQL Server community during our Tuesday Office Hours session. From the nuances of using merge statements to optimizing performance in integration tests and understanding query plans, I dive deep into practical solutions that can save you time and headaches. Whether you're dealing with sudden query spills or wondering about the merits of merge joins, this video covers a range of topics that are crucial for anyone working with SQL Server. If you have your own questions or need further clarification on any of these points, feel free to ask them in the comments below or through the provided link. Don't forget to like, subscribe, and share this video if you found it helpful!

items.title: AI Is Fast. AI Projects Are Slow. Let's Fix That.
items.author: MLOps.community
items.summary:
Joe Maionchi (Co-founder & COO) and Rod Christensen (Co-founder & Chief Architect) of RocketRide join the MLOps Community to walk through AIDE — the AI Integrated Development Environment. RocketRide is an open-source AI pipeline platform that lets developers build, debug, and run production-grade agentic AI workflows directly from their IDE, with support for 13+ LLM providers, 8+ vector databases, and full multi-agent orchestration.

AI Is Fast. AI Projects Are Slow. Let's Fix That. // MLOps Podcast #380 with JRocketRide's Joe Maionchi (Co-founder & COO) and Rod Christensen (Co-founder & Chief Architect)

A huge shout-out to @RocketRide-ai for this collaboration!

🔑 What's covered:
🏗️ Why AI infrastructure needs standardization — how coding agents produce inconsistent "glue code" across projects and why a typed node graph fixes it
⚡ Efficiency AI vs. Opportunity AI — the two paths companies take with generative AI and which one actually compounds growth
🔀 Multi-agent pipeline orchestration — running CrewAI, LangChain, and DeepAgent side-by-side to benchmark which works best for your use case
💰 Cutting LLM costs in half — design-time strategies for routing tasks to cheaper models without sacrificing output quality
🔍 Pipeline observability & debugging — logging every node step in dev and production so you can pinpoint exactly where a 10-step pipeline breaks
🖼️ Beyond text: image, video & audio nodes — frame grabbing, OCR, Whisper transcription, and speech-to-text running on shared GPU infrastructure
🚀 RocketRide Cloud — one-click deploy from local to cloud with dynamic GPU scaling and cost-efficient shared inference
🧠 Intentionality in agentic development — why moving fast with AI agents creates "crappy code fast" and how skills/context files change the equation
🔌 MCP support & framework-agnostic design — swap any model, tool, or framework without rewrites

This episode is essential for AI engineers, ML practitioners, and developers building production LLM applications who want to stop reinventing infrastructure and start shipping.

🔗 Links & Resources:

• RocketRide open source (GitHub): https://github.com/rocketride-org/rocketride-server
• AIDE VS Code Extension: https://rocketride.org
• MLOps Community: https://mlops.community

items.title: Office Hours: Database Q&A Off St. Thomas
items.author: Brent Ozar Unlimited
items.summary:
Got database questions? Post them for free at https://pollgab.com/room/brento. Here's what we covered on the balcony: 

00:00 Start
01:40 DbaMan: You have been reulctant to turn on ADR. It is required for optimized locing in SQL Server 2025. What is your view of ADR + Optimized locking? Is it almost an automatic yes, or should it only be enabled if we have BIG problems with locking/blocking?
05:32 TeaEarlGrayHot: Why is the size of the persistent version store in SQL with optimized locking a concern while in postgres and mysql that store their persistent version store in table, it is not? Is the assumption that postgres and mysql are less likely to use HA?
07:27 Will: We have a primary mssql enterprise cluster (2 vms) and a DR cluster (2 vms). We use one always on AG on the primary cluster, and another for the DR cluster. We connect the two AGs via a DAG. Is this a typical SQL DR setup, or is there a better way to set up a DR environment?
11:34 MyTeaGotCold: Have you seen anyone regret choosing Azure Hyperscale rather than another Azure PaaS? Microsoft seems to push it very hard.
12:25 Jeffry Altamar: What is your advice for removing a massive 4TB table from a live database: should I delete records in chunks and then drop it, or simply drop the table with no previous steps? What is safest?
13:47 Elwood Blues: How much AI should a prospective SQL 2025 DBA know if the database is using the new vector type?
15:33 Bandu: What's your opinion of AI written books?  Should they be flagged as AI witten? Would you ever purchase one?

items.title: Easy Migration from Postgres to Databricks Lakebase
items.author: Advancing Analytics
items.summary:
Migration projects always feel like they're going to be fraught with danger, but in the age of AI, it really shouldn't be. We can quickly build and configure custom validation engines, migration wizards, test harnesses and more, in blinding speed compared to the days of old. So that's what we've done with Databricks Lakebase.

If you're looking at taking an existing PostgreSQL Database and shifting it into Lakebase, it'll likely be fairly straightforward. But there a couple of gotchas that will trip you up if you don't plan ahead.

In this video, Simon walks through the various hazards, then shows a quick demo of the Advancing Lakebase Migration tool, shifting an example PostgreSQL database into Lakebase in a couple of minutes!

Tempted to port your existing database over? Give Advancing a shout
